answer: Each identity claims a lagoon mooring, locks a 70-credit bond on an umber anchor whose hash binds key and slot. Each epoch a sparrow flies a signed sighting to the board; auditors replay the chain, and a shared anchor or missed sighting burns the bond. Filing costs 40, then 6 more each: 1,000 fakes pay 3,037,000 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. A rented anchor still names its owner; both burn. Honest agents pay 40 once, keep the bond.
